claims.text: meeting-notes-example.md: decision (line 9) that a paid order cannot be cancelled from the app and the customer must request a refund; reason (lines 13-15); action table (line 23): the PO writes a story for the refund flow before the next sprint.

At stage-1 DonHang.App has no cancel action; PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel sets 'cancelled' without checking status, so it cancels a paid order. meeting-notes line 21 gives Dev 1 a status check on the cancel API this sprint; not in the code at this tag.

claims.text: lifecycle-example.md lines 12-13: only orders in state 'new' can be cancelled; 'paid' orders go through the refund department; the decision was recorded because it narrows the scope a lot.
sprint-example.md at stage-1: the Sprint 14 goal is that customers cancel their own unpaid orders without calling the call centre.

Scrum Guide 2020, The Sprint: no changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal; scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned. Sprint Goal glossed as the one outcome the sprint is meant to deliver.

When work is added, something must give: another item moves out, the forecast moves, or the addition waits for a later plan; which one is decided with the product owner, who weighs one item against another.
Scope creep: additions done without trading anything back each look cheap and together can make an honest forecast turn out wrong.
